review_notes: I read the whole file and the descendZ2 API in Inflation/Basic.lean. Most repeated material is short: the `hmul` group identities, the `add`/`sub` lift lemmas, and the `induction q/r using QuotientGroup.induction_on` boilerplate. The first finding below is the only repetition that is arguably more than routine, because the same trivialisation rewrite appears in three proofs. The second is the quotient-induction pattern, which is borderline routine. I did not run Lean, so the proposed lemmas and rewrites are untested. I did not search other files for further uses of either pattern.

findings.excerpt:
have hsmul : g • c (inverseConjugationHom N g n) = c n + ((n : G) • f g - f g) := by
    rw [← hconj]
    abel
findings.problem: Three proofs each restate the same conjugation-primitive identity. They convert `g • c (conj n) - c n = d0 N M A n` into `g • c (conj n) = c n + (n • A - A)`, or the equivalent `n • A = A + g • c (conj n) - c n`. Each does `rw [d0_apply, Subgroup.smul_def] at hconj`, states a local `have` (`hn` at 304, `hsmul` at 318, `hsmul` at 540), and closes it with `rw`/`abel`. The statement is re-derived with slightly different shapes and with `A` specialised to `f g` in two places.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one private lemma next to `smul_apply_one`, in the `Lift` section:
`theorem smul_conj_eq_of_sub_eq_d0 {c : N → M} {t : G} {A : M} (hA : ∀ n : N, t • c (inverseConjugationHom N t n) - c n = d0 N M A n) (n : N) : t • c (inverseConjugationHom N t n) = c n + ((n : G) • A - A)`.
Proof: `have h := hA n; rw [d0_apply, Subgroup.smul_def] at h; rw [← h]; abel`.
It needs no topology on `M`, so it can sit before `Lift` uses it. `d1_apply_coe_left` then uses it with `A := f g` and `hf.smul_conj_sub g`. `d1_apply_mul_left` uses the same lemma and rearranges it to get `hn`. `smul_conj_sub_mul` uses it with `A := A` in place of its `hsmul`. The two `hmul` commutation facts at 300 and 314/328 could be one lemma `(n : G) * g = g * inverseConjugationHom N g n` in the same place.
findings.benefit: The trivialisation rewrite is proved once and its meaning is stated once. The three proofs shrink to the rewrite chains that are actually specific to them. Any later change to `d0_apply` or to the `smul` convention on `N` is then made in one place.

findings.excerpt:
obtain ⟨q, r⟩ := p
  induction q using QuotientGroup.induction_on with | H g => ?_
  induction r using QuotientGroup.induction_on with | H k => ?_
  refine Subtype.ext ?_
findings.problem: Each of these proofs reduces an equality of `Z2 (G ⧸ N) (FixedPoints.addSubgroup N M)` cocycles, or of the functions that underlie them. It does so with the same 4-line sequence: destructure the pair, apply `QuotientGroup.induction_on` to both coordinates, and apply `Subtype.ext`. The sequence appears at 372-375, 381-384, 412-415 and 860-863. The first three come after a `Subtype.ext (funext ...)` header, so the whole skeleton is repeated.
findings.proposed_change: Add a lemma, for example `theorem Z2_quotient_ext {z z' : (G ⧸ N) × (G ⧸ N) → FixedPoints.addSubgroup N M} (h : ∀ g k : G, (z (g, k) : M) = z' (g, k)) : z = z'`, where `g k : G` are coerced into `G ⧸ N`. Proof: `funext ⟨q, r⟩`, then the induction on `q` and `r`, then `Subtype.ext (h g k)`. A bundled version for `Z2` would take `Subtype.ext` and apply the same lemma. `cocycle_add` and `cocycle_eq_zero` then reduce to `simp only [..., coe_cocycle_apply_mk, ...]`. `cocycle_sub_mem_B2` and `fiveTerm_exact_H2Q` use the function-level form directly.
findings.benefit: Callers state only the pointwise identity on representatives. The proofs of `cocycle_add` and `cocycle_eq_zero` become one or two lines. This is the usual way to work with `descendZ2` values, and the pattern is likely to recur in later files. It is a modest gain, since each repetition is boilerplate.
